chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Aasim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays who said:
I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying regarding a man who had four wives under him, so he divorced one, then married another before the divorced woman had completed her waiting period.
He said: So let him keep her with her family until the divorced woman completes her term, and the other one would face another waiting period.

And for her is her dower, if he had consummated the marriage with her. So, if he did not happen to have consummated the marriage with her, then for him is her wealth (dower), and there is no waiting period upon her.
Then, if her family so desires, after the expiration of her waiting period, to get her married (to him), and if they so desire, they do not get her married (to him).
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling when a man divorces one wife and marries another before the first wife's waiting period ends?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the validity of simultaneous marriages by treating the second union as a new contract with its own independent waiting period, rather than a continuation of the first. It highlights the practical legal distinction between consummated and non-consummated marriages regarding dower and iddah, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on the autonomy of each marital bond. The ruling underscores the family's authority in finalizing the transition, ensuring social and legal clarity for the divorced wife.
